angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,620,285 km at 22.84 pc = 0.95 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 162003: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 43.79 +/- 0.45 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 22.836 +/- 0.235 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 43.9500 +/- 0.8625 mas (same row, RUWE 3.43), 51.0 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 2.329 +/- 0.067 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 162003: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.949 +/- 0.026 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 2.329 +/- 0.067 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 1,620,285 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.311 +/- 0.016 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 162003: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.311 +/- 0.016 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6014 +/- 90 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 162003: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6014 +/- 90 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 162003: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6014 +/- 90 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/psi1-draconis-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.821, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
